transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I'm just here because I've been struggling a little bit lately. It's probably nothing major, but I just can't seem to shake this feeling that... well, that work just isn't a safe place for me anymore. And, I don't know, I just feel a little... damaged, I guess? Like the competent person who just got promoted isn't really there anymore. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Can you tell me more about this feeling that work isn't a safe place for you anymore?

Well, it's... I mean, I know it's probably silly of me to even bring it up. I've just been trying to manage things a little differently lately, you know, just to be careful. I don't want to be a burden on my team or anything, but I've started, um, trading some of my shifts with coworkers, and maybe pushing back on our release windows just a little bit. 

And I've been trying to work from home whenever I can... or at least taking the side entrance when I do have to go into the office. It's just... I'm sorry, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but if I have to walk through that main lobby after dark, I just get this awful feeling. Like I’m going to completely come apart. 

I know that sounds like a huge overreaction, and I'm really trying not to let it affect my performance. Is that... is it okay that I'm doing that for now? I hope I don't sound completely unreasonable.
Have you been avoiding any other places or situations besides the main lobby at work?

No, not really. I mean... I've been trying to just stick to my normal routine as much as possible. I don't want this to turn into a whole big thing where I'm, you know, hiding from the world or anything. So it's really just that one specific spot at work. Everything else is... well, it's fine. I'm still doing everything I normally do. I hope that's a good sign? Like maybe it's not as bad as I'm making it out to be?
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely get stressed out, especially lately, but... not like a sudden, intense panic or anything like that. I don't think I've ever had a full-blown panic attack, if that's what you mean. I usually just try to take a deep breath and keep going. I'm pretty good at holding it together in the moment, I think. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.
Has something specific happened to you at work that made you start feeling this way?

Well, um... yes. I guess I should have just said that from the beginning. I'm sorry, I just... I don't want to sound like I'm still dwelling on it, you know? Because it's been a while, and I feel like I should be completely over it by now. 

But, um, there was a break-in at the office. It was during an overnight deployment, so I was there late. And... well, that's when it happened. But that was, gosh, about two years and four months ago now. So it's really silly that I'm still getting so worked up about the lobby, isn't it? I mean, I know the building is secure now, and management handled everything really well. I just... I hope you don't think I'm being weak for still letting it bother me after all this time. Is it normal to still feel a little jumpy after that long?
Are you avoiding talking or thinking about the break-in at the office?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I try not to bring it up all the time because I don't want to be a bother or make anyone else uncomfortable. But if someone asks, I'll talk about it. And I definitely still think about it sometimes, but I really try to just push those thoughts away and focus on my work. I don't want it to seem like I'm obsessed with it or anything. I'm trying really hard to move past it, I promise. Is that the right way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing to get better.
Do you often think that you're not as capable or competent as you used to be?

Um, well... I guess I have been struggling with that a little bit. I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything, but... yeah. I just can't seem to shake this feeling that work isn't a safe place anymore. And... I don't know, it's almost like I feel a little bit damaged now? 

Like, I used to be so on top of things, and I worked really hard to get promoted, but lately I just feel like... like that competent person isn't really there anymore. I mean, I still get my work done, I really do! I'm trying my absolute best. But I just don't feel as sharp as I used to be. Is that... is that a normal thing to feel? I really hope I'm not just making excuses for myself. I want to be the employee I used to be, I really do.
Do you have memories of the break-in that still feel really vivid or disturbing to you?

Um... well, I really try not to let them get to me. I know I should be focusing on the present, and I don't want to sound dramatic. But, um... yes, I guess I do have some memories that pop up like that. I hope that doesn't mean I'm failing at moving on. 

Sometimes, if I hear a badge scanner beeping, or... or just heavy footsteps out in the hallway... or even if I get a late-night deployment alert... it's like I'm suddenly put right back in that office. My chest gets all tight, and... um... I'm sorry, I don't want to be too graphic or make you uncomfortable, but... I just get this sudden image of the guard on the floor. It just cuts right through whatever I’m doing. I really do try to shake it off right away and get back to work, I promise. Is it okay that I still get those flashes? I'm really trying my best to just push through them so I'm not a burden on my team.
Do you often think that you're worthless or inadequate as a person?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I definitely have my moments where I feel like I'm not doing as well at my job as I used to, like I mentioned, but... I don't think I'm worthless as a person. I know I still have good qualities, and I try really hard to be a good friend and a good employee. 

I mean, I hope I don't come across as someone who just feels sorry for themselves all the time. I'm really trying to keep a positive attitude about things, you know? I want to be someone who contributes and helps out. So, no, I don't feel worthless... I just feel a little off my game right now. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you often find yourself trying to avoid memories of the break-in?

Um... well, I really try not to let it affect my work too much, I promise. I want to be reliable for my team. But... I guess I have been making some adjustments lately? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee. 

It's just... I've started trading shifts when I can, or asking to push back on the late-night release windows. And, um, I try to work from home more often now, or I'll take the side entrance if I do have to go in. I just... walking through that main lobby after dark, it just makes me feel like I'm going to come apart, you know? I really try to push past it, but sometimes it's just easier to work around it so I can still get my job done. Is it okay that I'm doing that? I'm just trying to manage it the best way I know how without bothering anyone else.
Do you believe you're a different person now compared to who you were before the break-in?

Um... I really hate to admit this, because I want to be the same reliable person I've always been. I know I should just push through it and be grateful I'm okay. But... yes, I guess I do feel different. 

Honestly, it's a big part of why I'm here. I just... I can't seem to shake this feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And, um... I kind of feel like I'm somehow damaged now? I hope that doesn't make me sound weak, or like I'm just throwing a pity party for myself. It's just... I worked so hard for my career, and it feels like the competent person who got promoted recently just... isn't really there anymore. 

I'm trying so hard to get her back, I promise. I don't want to be like this forever. Is it normal that I feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm making sense and not overreacting to everything.
Do you believe you're less capable of achieving your goals now than you were before the break-in?

Um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm just giving up on everything, because I'm definitely not. I still want to advance in my career and do a really good job as an analyst. 

I know I'm struggling with the work environment right now, but... I don't feel like I'm incapable of reaching my goals eventually. I just need to figure out how to get back on track, you know? I still have my degree, I still have my technical skills... I really want to keep moving forward and prove I can still be successful. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure you know that I'm still trying my absolute best, even if I'm having a hard time right now. I haven't lost my drive or anything like that.
Do you believe you're less competent as a person now compared to before the break-in?

Um... well, I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I'm not. But... I guess I kind of touched on this a minute ago? It's just... I really feel like the capable, competent person who earned that promotion just... isn't really there right now. 

I know I shouldn't think like that, and I'm really trying to fix it so I can be the employee my team needs. But it's just so hard when I constantly feel like I'm damaged goods now, you know? Like I'm just broken somehow. I really hope that doesn't sound too dramatic or like I'm whining. I just... I want to be that competent person again so badly. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Do you often have memories of the break-in that feel disturbing to you?

Um... yeah. I try really hard to just push them out of my head, because I know I need to focus and do my job, but... they do pop up. I really hope it doesn't make me sound crazy, but little things will just set it off. 

Like, um, if I hear a badge scanner beeping, or... or heavy footsteps in the hallway? Even just a late-night deployment alert on my phone. When that happens, I just... I suddenly feel like I'm right back in that office. My chest gets all tight, and I just see the image of the guard on the floor... and it just cuts right through whatever I'm trying to do. 

I really try to snap out of it quickly so I don't bother anyone or let it affect my work too much. But it is really disturbing when it happens. Is it... is it normal to have things like a beeping scanner trigger that kind of reaction? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things properly and not, you know, making a big deal out of nothing.
Do you believe you're permanently changed for the worse because of the break-in?

Um... I really don't want to sound like a pessimist, because I'm usually a very positive person. I always try to look on the bright side of things. But... yeah, I guess I do feel that way sometimes. 

Like I was saying before, I just... I feel like I'm somehow damaged now. The person who earned that promotion, the one who was so focused and capable... it just feels like she isn't really there anymore. And I just can't shake this awful feeling that work isn't safe anymore, no matter how hard I try to tell myself otherwise. 

I'm really, really trying to get back to normal, though. I don't want to be permanently changed for the worse. I want to be the employee I used to be. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as too negative or like I'm not trying to get better, because I really am.
Do you try to avoid thinking about the break-in when memories of it come to your mind?

Um... yes. Like I mentioned, I really try to push those thoughts away so I can just focus. But, um... I feel a little silly admitting this, because I really don't want you to think I'm not dedicated to my job anymore. I am, I promise! 

But to keep from thinking about it, I've... well, I've started changing my routine a bit. I've been trading my evening shifts, and kind of pushing back on our late-night release windows. And... I've been taking the side entrance, or just working from home whenever they'll let me. It's just... walking through that main lobby after dark, it makes me feel like I'm going to completely come apart. 

I know avoiding it probably isn't the right way to handle things, and I really am going to try to stop doing that soon. I just want to keep being a good analyst without breaking down at work, you know? Is... is it okay that I'm avoiding the lobby like that for right now, just until I get better? I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible.
For how long have you been avoiding the main lobby at work?

Um... well, it's been a while, I guess. I mean, I really have been trying to force myself to just be normal about it, but... it's actually been going on since the break-in happened. Which was... um, during that overnight deployment about two years and four months ago. 

I know that sounds like a really long time to still be avoiding a lobby, and I probably should have gotten over it by now. I'm really sorry if that makes it seem like I'm not trying hard enough to move past it. I really am trying, I promise. Is it... is it really bad that it's been going on for that long? I just hope you don't think less of me for not being able to just walk through the front door like everyone else.
Do you often think that you are flawed or defective as a person because of what happened during the break-in?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I know I said earlier that I feel... well, a little damaged when it comes to work, but I don't think I'm, like, fundamentally flawed as a person. 

I really try to keep a good perspective on things. I know I'm still a good friend, and I still care about people, and I try to be kind... I don't think the break-in ruined who I am on the inside. I really hope it hasn't, anyway. I just have these... these struggles with work and the lobby right now, but I'm still me. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right. I definitely don't want you to think I've just completely given up on myself, because I haven't. I still believe I'm a good person.

target_item.manifestation: A badge scanner beeping, heavy footsteps in the hallway, or a late-night deployment alert can suddenly put me right back in that office, with my chest tight and the image of the guard on the floor cutting through whatever I’m doing.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disturbing memories of the break-in, which directly relates to the intrusive symptoms described in my profile.

patient.answer:
Um... yeah. I try really hard to just push them out of my head, because I know I need to focus and do my job, but... they do pop up. I really hope it doesn't make me sound crazy, but little things will just set it off. 

Like, um, if I hear a badge scanner beeping, or... or heavy footsteps in the hallway? Even just a late-night deployment alert on my phone. When that happens, I just... I suddenly feel like I'm right back in that office. My chest gets all tight, and I just see the image of the guard on the floor... and it just cuts right through whatever I'm trying to do. 

I really try to snap out of it quickly so I don't bother anyone or let it affect my work too much. But it is really disturbing when it happens. Is it... is it normal to have things like a beeping scanner trigger that kind of reaction? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things properly and not, you know, making a big deal out of nothing.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of persistent negative beliefs about oneself
doctor.question: Do you believe you're permanently changed for the worse because of the break-in?

target_item.name: Negative_Beliefs
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t shake the feeling that work isn’t safe anymore and that I’m somehow damaged now, like the competent person who got promoted isn’t really there anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I believe I am permanently changed for the worse, which relates to persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs about myself, covered by S072.

patient.answer:
Um... I really don't want to sound like a pessimist, because I'm usually a very positive person. I always try to look on the bright side of things. But... yeah, I guess I do feel that way sometimes. 

Like I was saying before, I just... I feel like I'm somehow damaged now. The person who earned that promotion, the one who was so focused and capable... it just feels like she isn't really there anymore. And I just can't shake this awful feeling that work isn't safe anymore, no matter how hard I try to tell myself otherwise. 

I'm really, really trying to get back to normal, though. I don't want to be permanently changed for the worse. I want to be the employee I used to be. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as too negative or like I'm not trying to get better, because I really am.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of avoidance of internal reminders
doctor.question: Do you try to avoid thinking about the break-in when memories of it come to your mind?

target_item.name: Trauma_Avoidance
target_item.manifestation: I’ve started trading shifts, pushing back on release windows, and taking the side entrance or working from home whenever I can because walking through that lobby after dark makes me feel like I’m going to come apart.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about avoiding thoughts or memories related to the break-in, which falls under Trauma Avoidance.

patient.answer:
Um... yes. Like I mentioned, I really try to push those thoughts away so I can just focus. But, um... I feel a little silly admitting this, because I really don't want you to think I'm not dedicated to my job anymore. I am, I promise! 

But to keep from thinking about it, I've... well, I've started changing my routine a bit. I've been trading my evening shifts, and kind of pushing back on our late-night release windows. And... I've been taking the side entrance, or just working from home whenever they'll let me. It's just... walking through that main lobby after dark, it makes me feel like I'm going to completely come apart. 

I know avoiding it probably isn't the right way to handle things, and I really am going to try to stop doing that soon. I just want to keep being a good analyst without breaking down at work, you know? Is... is it okay that I'm avoiding the lobby like that for right now, just until I get better? I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible.

doctor.intent: Determine the duration of avoidance behaviors
doctor.question: For how long have you been avoiding the main lobby at work?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on since the break-in during that overnight deployment about 2 years and 4 months ago.
target_item.reason: The doctor's last question asks 'For how long have you been avoiding the main lobby at work?', which directly asks about the duration of the symptoms.

patient.answer:
Um... well, it's been a while, I guess. I mean, I really have been trying to force myself to just be normal about it, but... it's actually been going on since the break-in happened. Which was... um, during that overnight deployment about two years and four months ago. 

I know that sounds like a really long time to still be avoiding a lobby, and I probably should have gotten over it by now. I'm really sorry if that makes it seem like I'm not trying hard enough to move past it. I really am trying, I promise. Is it... is it really bad that it's been going on for that long? I just hope you don't think less of me for not being able to just walk through the front door like everyone else.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of persistent negative beliefs about oneself
doctor.question: Do you often think that you are flawed or defective as a person because of what happened during the break-in?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling flawed or defective (Negative Beliefs, S072), which I already fully addressed in my first turn when I explained feeling damaged and that the competent person I used to be isn't there anymore. Therefore, I should return None as this has already been covered.

patient.answer:
Um... no, not really. I mean, I know I said earlier that I feel... well, a little damaged when it comes to work, but I don't think I'm, like, fundamentally flawed as a person. 

I really try to keep a good perspective on things. I know I'm still a good friend, and I still care about people, and I try to be kind... I don't think the break-in ruined who I am on the inside. I really hope it hasn't, anyway. I just have these... these struggles with work and the lobby right now, but I'm still me. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right. I definitely don't want you to think I've just completely given up on myself, because I haven't. I still believe I'm a good person.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms and history are consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), including avoidance of the main lobby at work due to a past traumatic event (the break-in), distressing memories of the event, and a persistent feeling of being 'damaged' or less competent as a person.
